title: Sampling Rate Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Audio
Sampling Rate
Nyquist Limit
Aliasing
Data Rate
description: Interactive p5.js MicroSim that samples a sine wave at a chosen rate and bit depth, rebuilds it as a DAC staircase, and shows the Nyquist limit, aliasing, and the data rate in bytes per second.

educational.topic: Audio sampling rate, Nyquist limit and aliasing
learningObjectives: Analyze how the sampling rate changes the number of samples per cycle and the shape of the rebuilt wave
Predict the heard frequency when a tone is above the Nyquist limit
Calculate the data rate of digital audio from the sampling rate, bit depth and channel count

keyQuestions: Why must the sampling rate be more than twice the highest frequency?
What frequency do you hear when a 3,500 Hz tone is sampled 4,000 times per second?
Why does doubling the bit depth double the data rate?
commonMisconceptions: A higher-frequency tone sampled too slowly just sounds quieter (it actually sounds like a different, lower pitch)
Exactly two samples per cycle is always enough (at exactly the Nyquist limit the samples can all land on zero)
assessmentOpportunities: State the Nyquist limit for a given sampling rate
Predict and verify an aliased frequency
Calculate bytes per second for a given rate and bit depth

controls.label: Show the wave you hear (after filtering)
